title: ONCat and data access
summary: Where run metadata comes from, what your login covers, and where the files live.
body:
# ONCat and data access

## One credential

ORNL neutron users hold a single **XCAMS** or **UCAMS** identity. The same
username and password covers ONCat, the monitor pages and IPTS. NeutronDesk
asks for it once and keeps it in the device secure store (iOS Keychain,
Android Keystore). It is sent only to ORNL services.

NeutronDesk acts with **your** permissions. It cannot show you an IPTS you
would not be able to open yourself, and it does not try to.

## What ONCat holds

ONCat is the catalogue, not the data. For each run it records:

- run number, title, start and end time, duration
- total counts and accumulated proton charge
- DAS logs: detector position, wavelength, chopper speed, sample environment
- the path of the raw NeXus file on the archive

Some of this is public. Run **metadata** requires an authenticated request,
which is why the Runs list needs you to be signed in.

## Where files live

Raw data follows a fixed convention:

    /SNS/EQSANS/IPTS-<number>/nexus/EQSANS_<run>.nxs.h5

Shared instrument files (sensitivity, dark current, beam flux) live under:

    /SNS/EQSANS/shared/NeXusFiles/EQSANS/<cycle>/

Reduced output goes wherever the reduction was told to write it, which is
outside the catalogue. NeutronDesk lists the raw file for a run and does not
guess at output paths.

## Units worth remembering

ONCat reports `detectorz` in **millimetres**. NeutronDesk converts to metres
before showing it, so a 4 m configuration reads as 4.000 m and not 4000.
